text:
oncall-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT CREATED — ID INC-20260315-73. Multiple prompt-processor-prod pods reporting OOMKilled and crashlooping in eu-west-1. Paging @infra-oncall @eng-sre

Sara: seeing the first failures at ~10:12 UTC. pod prompt-processor-prod-57 restarted with OOMKilled. CPU goes to 100% then kernel OOM kills the main process.

Ajay: metrics: request qps fairly normal but p95 CPU per pod spikes correlating with large prompts (long system instructions). suspect prompt splitting logic causing exponential work on some inputs.

Maria: started a manual scale from 4 -> 8 replicas to buy time, but restarts still happen after new pods hit the same workload. scaling only delays symptom.

Mohit: logs from the failing pod:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:41Z] ERROR prompt_processor.worker: failed to tokenize input
MemoryError: Unable to allocate 512MB for tokenizer buffer
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/prompt_processor/worker.py", line 214, in run
    tokens = tokenizer.encode_long(prompt)
  File "/app/tokenizer/utils.py", line 89, in encode_long
    buffer = bytearray(size_needed)
MemoryError
```
This looks like CPU-side memory exhaustion during chunking, not GPU.

Infra-oncall: starting a small canary patch to set PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT and bump container memory request to 3Gi for one pod. Applying patch to prompt-processor-prod-101 now. command: `kubectl patch deployment/prompt-processor -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"prompt-processor","resources":{"requests":{"memory":"3Gi"}}}]}}}}'`

Eng-sre: also seeing occasional cuda driver warnings on a different stack (decode path) but not the primary failure here. log sample: `cuda: driver callback timeout` — we should track separately. primary incident is CPU OOM in prompt preproc.

Sara: customer impact: error rate up from 0.3% -> 7.9% for chat endpoints in eu-west-1 starting 10:12, several active customers reporting failures (CS-3442, CS-3445). Some responses returned 502 / empty body.

Ajay: short-term mitigation: enable prefix KV caching and strict chunk guardrails (PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT=1024, MAX_TOKENS_PREP=8192). Also drop very large system messages to fallback handler that returns 413 with guidance instead of attempting full tokenize. Patch config snippet:
```yaml
- name: PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT
  value: "1024"
- name: MAX_TOKENS_PREP
  value: "8192"
- name: LARGE_PROMPT_FALLBACK
  value: "true"
```
This prevents pathological expansion on insane inputs.

Infra-oncall: canary pod (prompt-processor-prod-101) patched and healthy for 4m, CPU stabilised ~20%. rolling update to remaining replicas in progress (batch=2).

Maria: will open SEV ticket and notify affected customers with ETA to full rollback/patch. notifying Growth and CS.

Eng-sre: runbook steps executed: 1) scale up to absorb load (done), 2) cordon+drain node euw1-prep-3 (evicted a bad pod), 3) apply canary config, 4) enable autoscaler override to 12 replicas for 30m. Keep a close eye on p95 latency. Commands I ran: `kubectl cordon euw1-prep-3 && kubectl drain euw1-prep-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force`

Sara: handoff note for night: impacts subsided but we saw elevated error budgets for some customers. CS ticket links: https://redwood/cs/3442 and https://redwood/cs/3445. Root cause suspected: a combination of an upstream client sending unbounded system prompts + tokenizer fallback path that allocates large buffers per chunk.

Oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: @mike will take on-call at 18:00 UTC. Please add any outstanding actions to the handoff list.

Mike: ack. I will keep autoscaler override and the patch in place until tomorrow morning 08:00 UTC, monitor OOMs and 5xx rates, and run an additional load test with long prompts against the canary.

Maria: Post-incident actions (initial):
- Add guardrail to gateway to reject >200k char system prompts (product ask)
- Harden tokenizer to stream/iterate without allocating huge contiguous buffers
- Add unit/e2e test with adversarial long prompts to CI
- Improve alerting: fire a separate CPU-OOM alert for prompt-processor with runbook link
- Track follow-up on CUDA warnings separately

Mike: noted. tagging @infra-oncall and @eng-sre for next steps. I'll post a short incident summary to #incidents-summary after midnight.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — status: mitigated (rolling patch active). Will remain monitored.
